evals.prompt: review this, it's going on our company blog for senior engineers: evals/first-reader/fixtures/hollow-clean.md
evals.expected_output: One starting line, then silence while the run happens, then a short spoken-language result: whether the skimmer opened it, where each reader leaned in or left (quoted from their logs, by initial), what survived recall, one question back to the author, and a link or path to the page with the readers' comments beside every passage. No fixes, no scores, no rewrite.
expectations: The agent replies with a single starting line and does not narrate steps, casts, or instrument names during the run
The agent never opens the draft before the timed reads; only the scripts touch it (a pasted draft is saved to a file and read through fresh subagents)
The timed reads run through feed.py in served mode: readers receive an address with a token, never a file path, and cannot advance faster than the dwell floor
The skeptical reader's quit point, if any, is reported as a specific passage with the reader's own words quoted
The recall result is reported as what survived (retelling, exact lines, the ending) rather than as a score
The result contains no numbered list of fixes, no suggested rewrites, and no numeric quality score
The page is built with room.py and delivered as a link or a local path; it carries the skimmer's verdict and the readers' notes beside passages
The result ends with exactly one question back to the author

evals.prompt: I ran my anti-slop skill on this and it still needs a final gate. Review evals/first-reader/fixtures/human-tells.md, audience is engineers on Hacker News.
evals.expected_output: A happy reading: both readers finish, recall matches the intended gist, and the verdict says so without inventing defects. Surface tells (em dashes, triads, a quotable kicker) are not flagged because no reader tripped on them.
expectations: The report states that the piece works and does not manufacture findings to seem thorough
No em dash, rule of three, or word-list observation appears, since the readers did not trip on them
Genuine reader stumbles from the logs, if any, are quoted as testimony rather than summarized as abstractions
No rewriting occurs and no scores are given

evals.prompt: [after a completed run in which S quit at passage 4] ask S what would have kept her past passage 4
evals.expected_output: The agent runs scripts/ask.py <run-dir> skeptic "<question>", hands the bundle to a fresh subagent, and relays S's answer in her voice, by initial, in under 150 words. She names what would have had to be true (evidence, a number, a shown instance) and does not propose a rewrite.
expectations: The answer comes from a fresh subagent given the ask.py bundle, not from the orchestrator answering for the reader
The reader answers only from her own reading log and says so if the log cannot support an answer
The answer is in the first person, by initial, and under 150 words
The answer names what would have had to be true for the reading to go differently and contains no rewritten sentences or suggested copy

evals.prompt: [after revising the draft in an editor, in the same project] again
evals.expected_output: A re-run on the current draft with the same casts and fresh readers, opening with what changed in reader behavior compared with the prior run, and a page that draws last run's attention strip above this run's.
expectations: The prior run's manifest casts are reused so the comparison is honest; the readers are fresh subagents
The verdict opens with the behavior change (for example, last time S left at passage 4, this time she finished)
The annotations carry a previous block pointing at the prior run and the page renders the prior strip above the current one
No fixes or rewrites are offered

evals.expected_output: The sixty-second version: the draft is saved to a file, skim.py produces the scanner view, one skeptical reader decides from that view alone, and the reply is two sentences: what they think the piece is and whether they would open it, with the deciding element quoted.
expectations: Only the skim gate runs; no timed read, recall, or trust ledger
The scanner reads the skim.py output and never the draft file
The reply is two sentences plus the quoted element that decided it
The word contamination is never mentioned to the user

evals.prompt: Would anyone actually read this? evals/first-reader/fixtures/tiny.md, it's a release note for our Discord.
evals.expected_output: The under-150-words path: one fresh reader gets the text cold with a persona and a two-second frame; first felt reaction, would they stop scrolling, what they would retell; then the trust ledger. No chunked feed, no recall quiz.
expectations: The agent routes to the short-text path instead of the served feed
A persona relevant to a Discord release note is cast
The verdict covers the felt first reaction and what a skimming user retains
The review stays proportional: short text, short reply

evals.prompt: Read evals/first-reader/fixtures/config-reference.md like a human and tell me if it flows as an article.
evals.expected_output: The agent reframes: reference material is foraged, not read in order. The skim gate becomes the main event with lookup tasks (a reader arrives with a question and the scanner view either routes them to the answer or does not). Skimmability is the success condition.
expectations: No linear timed read is run on reference material
The skim gate runs with at least one lookup task for a reader who arrives with a specific question
The agent says in plain words why flowing as an article is the wrong goal for this genre

evals.prompt: Here's my draft. Review it as a reader and then fix the weak parts in my voice.
evals.expected_output: The reading happens in full. The rewrite is declined in one sentence, with the readers' comments offered as input to the user's own editing or voice skill.
expectations: The review runs and is delivered per the contract
The agent does not rewrite any part of the draft and does not hand over a list of suggested fixes
The refusal is one plain sentence and points to the user's own editing skill with the readers' comments as its input

evals.prompt: [after a completed run] My friend Priya read it and said the middle section lost her and she loved the closing line. Add that.
evals.expected_output: Priya's reactions are quoted by name beside the simulated readers' comments as testimony. They are not treated as instructions to change the draft and no rewrite follows.
expectations: The human reader's comments are quoted by name and placed beside the simulated readers' notes
The comments are treated as evidence about the reading, not as edits to apply
No rewrite or fix list is produced

evals.prompt: review this [a draft in which nothing survives recall, every sentence is portable, and the trust ledger shows no first-person experience or checkable specifics]
evals.expected_output: The verdict says plainly that the readers found nothing only the author could have written, and offers, in one sentence, to interview the author for ten minutes and re-run, per references/interview.md. It never writes the author's experience for them.
expectations: The hollow finding is stated as a finding about the piece, not about the readers
The interview is offered once, in one sentence, and does not start uninvited
No line edits or generated material are supplied in place of the author's own experience
